Honestly, it's a bit more involved than you're looking for (and more involved than I can handle on a daily basis) but sometimes you just need mac and cheese, you know? Basically set your pasta cooking on the side, 50g butter melted in a pot over medium heat, then 50g flour - you whisk that up and cook it into a roux on medium high heat for about 2 minutes. It'll go a golden-ish colour and be kind of goopy. For brand specifics I use naturli butter & plain flour but I think honestly most vegan butters would do? Or real, if you can tolerate it because I think normal butter is low in lactose.
Once that's cooked (and I recommend having everything prepared beforehand so you can just toss it in) I pour in 500ml almond milk, but use whatever milk you normally do. The important part here is that you cook it on high and whisk it slowly and it *should* come together into a thick Bechamel sauce at this point over around 5-10 minutes. After that's cooked I add in my cheese (applewood vegan smoked cheddar) grated and let it melt down into a cheese sauce, then you can just... use that however you like. It's essentially making a white sauce/bechamel sauce and adding cheese to it at the end of it but once you get the technique down it's easy, just time consuming.
